lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 2]: Reader knows Lane left Ole Miss for LSU, tonight's return to Oxford, top-10 matchup stakes. New today: final result (Ole Miss 32-24), Chambliss's dominance (325+ pass yds, 2+ pass TD, go-ahead rush TD, sealing INT), the halftime blowout (24-7), LSU's rally that fell short, the postgame emotion (Chambliss cursed on live TV: 'HOTTY F*CKING TODDY'), and the revenge angle completed. Skip the backstory — reader saw it yesterday. Lead with the result and the dominance: Chambliss has now had 3 games with 325+ pass yds and 2+ pass TD since Kiffin left (in just 6 games) vs 2 such games in 11 games under Kiffin per StatMuse — he is THRIVING without Lane. The Ole Miss fans made Kiffin's arrival hell (lined staircases, booed him relentlessly), the ESPN cut from Holly Rowe to Laura Rutledge was diabolical per HaterReport, Chambliss looking at Lane after beating him, the cameraman zooming in on Lane after every Ole Miss TD. This wasn't just a win — it was a statement. Chambliss is the new king of Oxford. Lane got the belt, and the internet loved every second of it. Cross-sport irony: this is the ex-revenge-game beat perfected — the player you left behind thriving, the new team you left for struggling, the hostile return that goes exactly wrong. Name the other great ex-revenge games in sports history (LeBron's first game back in Cleveland as a Cavalier, Brady's Bucs beating the Pats, etc.) — this is in that lineage. The meme potential: Lane's face after every Ole Miss score, Chambliss walking into Ole Miss frat parties tonight as the new god, the 'When Lane Kiffin loses, America wins' energy. Ranking Lane's coaching stops by how badly they ended (Oakland, Tennessee, USC, FAU, Ole Miss to LSU) — where does this rank? The stat: Chambliss now has the same number of 325+ pass yd / 2+ pass TD games in SIX games post-Kiffin as he had in ELEVEN under Kiffin. That's not random — that's a QB unleashed. The Heisman race just got interesting: Chambliss is now the frontrunner per CBS Sports, surging past everyone else with this performance. The historical angle: Lane Kiffin is one of the few coaches who gets BOOED by his own former fanbase — how rare is that? Most coaches leave on good terms or quietly. Lane left Ole Miss mid-contract for LSU and Oxford has not forgiven him. The crowd energy tonight was PERSONAL. The coaching angle: Pete Golding (Ole Miss DC) postgame: 'I think Keith Carter and Glenn Boyce might have a beer tonight' per SportsCenter — those are the Ole Miss AD and chancellor who Lane left behind. They just watched their replacement coach get embarrassed by the team Lane abandoned. The Lane Kiffin coaching tree is now 0-1 against the schools he left. The final beat: Chambliss sealed it with an interception — LSU had the ball, a chance to make it close, and Chambliss (who already had the go-ahead rushing TD) took it away himself. That's a two-way performance in a revenge game. The internet reaction was INSTANT: 'Lane Kiffin running to his private jet as soon as the clock hit zero' per NFLMemes, 'Trinidad Chambliss walking into Ole Miss frat parties tonight' per ghetto_gronk, 'When Lane Kiffin loses, America wins' per NFLMemes. This was appointment viewing, and the result delivered.

supporting_stories.headline: Gable Steveson's UFC Debut Lasted 12 Seconds
supporting_stories.research_notes: Gable Steveson — Olympic gold medalist wrestler, hyped UFC debut — got knocked out COLD by Sean Sharaf 12 seconds into UFC 331 per LeBatardShow/HaterReport/SportsCenter. Left hook, lights out per HaterReport. Jon Jones (UFC GOAT) watched in horror per HaterReport. This is an all-time upset and an all-time disaster debut. The hype: Steveson was supposed to be the next Brock Lesnar — Olympic gold, NCAA champ, freak athlete transitioning to MMA. The reality: he got starched before the crowd even sat down. The stat: 12 seconds. That's faster than most people can microwave popcorn. The cross-sport comp: this is like if LeBron's NBA debut ended with him getting dunked on and benched in the first minute. The meme angle: Jon Jones' face says it all — he was there to support the new generation of wrestler-to-MMA stars, and instead watched a catastrophe. The wrestling-to-MMA track record: Lesnar succeeded, Daniel Cormier succeeded, Henry Cejudo succeeded — Steveson just became the cautionary tale. The internet reaction was SAVAGE: 'Gable Steveson on the way home after his fight with Sean Sharaf' (video of someone walking dejectedly) per HaterReport, 'Sean Sharaf put Gable Steveson TO SLEEP in the first 10 seconds. INSANE' per HaterReport. This is a career-defining moment for both fighters — Sharaf just became a star, Steveson just became a meme. The comeback question: can Steveson recover from this? Or is his UFC career over before it started? Compare to other disastrous UFC debuts (CM Punk getting destroyed, etc.) — this is up there. The night also had Arman Tsarukyan brutally KO'ing Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow, calling for a title shot per LeBatardShow/SportsCenter — but Steveson's loss is the story everyone will remember.

supporting_stories.research_notes: Three walkoff homers in one night across MLB: Ethan Salas (20 years old) pinch-hit walkoff for Padres 7-6 over Marlins per TalkinBaseball/ClutchPoints, Pavin Smith walkoff HR for Dbacks beat Yankees 5-3 on night celebrating 2001 WS team per TalkinBaseball, Christian Moore walkoff hit in 11th for Angels beat Twins 6-5 per ClutchPoints. The Salas angle: he's 20 years old, came in cold off the bench, and won it per TalkinBaseball — that's a CLUTCH rookie moment. The Dbacks angle: they were celebrating the 25th anniversary of the 2001 World Series team (Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling hoisted the trophy together before the game per TalkinBaseball), scoreboards were altered to look like 2001 per TalkinBaseball, and then Pavin Smith delivered a storybook ending against the Yankees (the team they beat in 2001) per TalkinBaseball. That's CINEMA. The Angels angle: they were down to their final strike TWICE — Vaughn Grissom tied it in the 9th off Mason Miller with a solo shot per ClutchPoints, then Christian Moore ended it in the 11th per ClutchPoints. The stat: three walkoffs in one night is rare but not unprecedented — but the DRAMA of each one (rookie debut hero, anniversary celebration revenge, double-comeback win) made this night special. The Padres also had Griffin Conine tie the game in the 9th off Mason Miller (one of MLB's best closers) before Salas ended it per TalkinBaseball — so the Padres needed TWO ninth-inning rallies to win. The cross-sport comp: this is like an NFL Sunday where every game ends on a Hail Mary — the walkoffs just kept coming. The meme angle: 'LET'S FUCKING GO SAN DIEGO' per JomboyMedia after Salas' hit. The historical Dbacks moment: Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling (2001 co-MVPs) together again, 25 years later, with the trophy — and then the team beats the Yankees in dramatic fashion. You can't script it better. The Angels' resilience: they were dead twice, came back both times, and won in extras. That's a character win. The Padres are now tied with the Dbacks for the final NL Wild Card spot per yesterday's content — so Salas' walkoff has playoff implications.

supporting_stories.topic: NC State fumbles intentional safety, Vanderbilt scores TD on return to win 35-31 — all-time ending in college football
supporting_stories.headline: NC State Tried An Intentional Safety And Lost The Game
supporting_stories.research_notes: NC State led Vanderbilt 31-28, attempted an intentional safety to run out the clock, fumbled the snap, Vanderbilt returned it for a touchdown to win 35-31 per ground truth/JomboyMedia/PatMcAfeeShow/SharpFootball/CBS Sports. Vandy never led all game until the FINAL PLAY per SharpFootball. This is an ALL-TIME college football ending — the kind that gets replayed for decades. The intentional safety strategy: NC State wanted to take a 2-point safety (making it 33-28), kick off from the 20, and force Vandy to drive the length of the field with no timeouts. It's a SMART call in theory — you give up 2 points but get better field position on the kickoff and keep the clock running. The execution: NC State fumbled the snap, Vanderbilt scooped it and scored, 35-31 final. The magnitude: this is the kind of loss that HAUNTS a program. NC State was in control, had the game won, and lost on a self-inflicted disaster. The meme angle: 'THAT'S AN OH NO HALL OF FAME' per PatMcAfeeShow, 'ABSOLUTELY INSANE WAY TO LOSE' per SharpFootball, 'INSANE — NC State went for an intentional safety and instead fumbled and lost the game to Vanderbilt' per JomboyMedia. The aftermath: NC State QB CJ Bailey is now under investigation for gambling-related policies, temporarily suspended per BallsackSports — the university is seeking to clear him by Monday per BallsackSports. So this disaster play is now ALSO tied to a potential scandal. The historical comp: this is up there with the Michigan punter fumbling the snap vs Michigan State in 2015, the Cal-Stanford lateral game, the Auburn kick-six — it's an instant classic disaster. The Vanderbilt angle: they were NEVER ahead until the final second per SharpFootball — this is the ultimate come-from-behind win without ever leading. The CBS Sports headline: 'Where Vanderbilt's stunning win over NC State ranks among the craziest endings since 2000' — it's THAT level. The internet loved it: every meme account, every highlight account, every college football fan saw this and lost their minds. The rule: intentional safeties are rare and risky — this is why. The NC State side: they had the right idea, the execution failed, and now it's a meme forever.
